To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the optimal constants of certain trace inequalities on $$\mathbb{S}^d$$Sd are stable, (ii) the optimal constants for the Hardy–Littlewood-Sobolev inequality in $$L^q(\mathbb{S})$$Lq(S) with $$q \ge 2$$q≥2 are stable, and (iii) the local version of Carlem’s duality theorem holds.

(i) the trace theorem on the sphere is stable with respect to small deformations of the sphere; (ii) the trace theorem into any $$L^q, q > 2$$Lq,q>2, is stable with respect the the Hardy–Littlewood-Sobolev inequality; and (iii) local stability of Strichartz estimates holds for the kinetic transport operator, with a loss of one derivative in the estimate for the remainder.
• The trace theorem into $$\ell_2^s$$ℓ2s for $$s \geq 1$$s≥1 is stable with optimal constants.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the sphere is a very well-behaved manifold from the point of view of stability of trace inequalities, which makes it a good testing ground for the study of more general manifolds.
